Use FEniCS legacy (dolfin) to solve a quasi-incompressible finite-strain hyperelasticity problem in plane strain using a mixed displacement-pressure neo-Hookean formulation solved with Newton's method.
The domain is a rectangular strip of dimensions 1.0 m by 0.20 m with two circular holes of radius 0.04 m centered at (0.40, 0.10) m and (0.60, 0.10) m.
Generate a triangular mesh with a maximum element size of approximately 0.01 m, ensuring the hole boundaries are well resolved.
The unknowns are the displacement field u = (u_x, u_y) and the hydrostatic pressure field p.
The material is an isotropic quasi-incompressible neo-Hookean solid with Young's modulus E = 5 MPa and Poisson's ratio nu = 0.49, giving shear modulus mu = E / (2(1+nu)) and Lamé parameter lambda = E / (3(1-2nu)).
The plane-strain assumption applies with unit thickness in the z-direction.
The left edge at x = 0 is fully fixed: u_x = 0 and u_y = 0.
The right edge at x = 1.0 has prescribed displacement u_x = 0.060 m and u_y = 0.
The top and bottom edges are traction-free.
Each hole boundary carries a uniform pressure of 0.10 MPa directed radially outward from the hole center into the solid.
The pressure traction on each hole boundary is applied using the outward reference normal of the undeformed hole, not the current (deformed) normal.
Use a mixed displacement-pressure weak form consistent with quasi-incompressibility in plane strain, where the pressure acts as a Lagrange multiplier enforcing the volumetric constraint.
Solve the nonlinear system using Newton's method with a standard convergence tolerance and a maximum iteration count sufficient for convergence.
Save a colour map of the pressure field p as a PNG file named q14_p.png.
Compute the von Mises stress from the Cauchy stress tensor and save a colour map as a PNG file named q14_vm.png.
Export the displacement field in XDMF format.
